This is a scene depicting a complete upheaval throughout the entire universe. Revolution has broken out among all existing things; this upheaval envelops the celestial bodies and this earth. Wild animals and domestic animals are also affected by it. The human soul and its movements have changed; every unknown reality is before the eyes and every secret has been laid bare. Man stands before his earnings and his provision for the journey, the reckoning and accounting has begun, and he is bewildered and distressed, for everything around him has been caught in this great storm, and the entire system of the universe has been thrown into turmoil.

These great cosmic events point to the fact that this beautiful and magnificent universe and its system, whose every movement is harmonious and ordered, whose structure is extremely firm, whose inner attraction is perfectly balanced, and which was created by the hands of One who is All-Knowing and All-Wise, will be scattered and dispersed; the bond of this firm system will be unfastened. The forces and qualities by which it is moving in this way will all cease, and in short this entire present system will be shattered, and then this universe and its creatures will attain a new life. This new universe and this new life will differ from the present characteristics.

This is the concept which this surah seeks to establish in the heart and sight, so that man may reflect and human consciousness may turn away from these apparent and temporary scenes, even though at first glance they appear very strong and contain within them the realities that remain. Man should contemplate the Being of Allah, who is abiding and everlasting, and who will still be abiding when this entire universe has passed away and mighty events have altered its very form. The purpose of this surah is that man should emerge from the sphere of this apparent, habitual and merely visible universe and attach himself to that absolute Reality and the Being of Allah, who is beyond time and space, beyond human perception and imagination, and who is not confined within any sphere or limit.

This is the true consciousness that arises within us when a person sees these great scenes of revolution in this surah. Through this observation, a trembling, as it were, overtakes a person, and the consciousness of Allah's greatness settles in the mind.

But what will actually happen? Knowledge of that belongs to Allah alone. Our consciousness and our imagination are very limited. Today we cannot fully conceive of these great upheavals. At most we can think that a great earthquake will take place on this earth, and this earthquake will bring destruction everywhere, and from within the earth there will be an uncontrollable volcanic activity, and planets and stars will fall upon the earth, piece by piece, and the water of the seas will take the form of a tempest, and also within the sun there will be volcanic activity, and its flames will rise for millions of miles, and man may even be able to see these observations.

But the cosmic upheavals that will occur at the establishment of the Resurrection, compared to this, our thinking, these ideas and these observations are mere consolations for children. If it is necessary for us to understand them, we can only bring expressions that present a general and approximate concept of these events, because beyond that we can do nothing else.

*Idhash-shamsu kuwwirat* (81:1): "When the sun is wrapped up." Its meaning may be that it will cool down and the agitation burning within it will come to an end. At present the process of burning within the sun is ongoing, and the flames that are rising from it rise thousands of miles around it. When a solar eclipse occurs, this process is clearly visible through observatories. Its meaning also includes that, through this burning process of the sun, all the material upon the sun turns into a flying gaseous form, and this gas rises into the burning atmosphere of the sun. This state will not remain thus, and the sun will cool down in the same way that this earth of ours has cooled, and there is no longer any incandescent process upon it. Beyond this, the surah may have other meanings which are not yet within our knowledge. How these processes will come into being is known only to Allah.

"And when the stars fall, scattering" (81:2). That is, they will break out of the system of bonds that exists in this universe and binds them all together. Their light will be extinguished and they will become dark. Only Allah knows which stars this event will befall. Will it be all the stars, or a group of stars that are close to us? For example, will it happen among the stars nearest to the sun, or in our galaxy, which contains tens of millions of stars? It will happen among all the stars, whose positions and orbits Allah knows, and whose number Allah knows too, because beyond what our observatories reach in our observation, there are countless other worlds. Our belief is that the stars will lose their light or scatter, and the full reality is known only to Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 81, verse 3:

[The passage begins with the verse quoted in full, as the commentary introduces it:]

﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ (81:3)

The meaning of the mountains being set in motion is, firstly, that they will be broken into pieces, ground to dust and scattered into the air, as is stated in another surah.

﴿They ask you about the mountains; say, "My Lord will blow them away as dust."﴾ (20:105)

And elsewhere:

﴿And the mountains will be broken into pieces and become scattered dust.﴾ (56:5–6)

And:

﴿And the mountains will be set in motion until they become a mirage.﴾ (78:20)

In all these verses there is an indication that the mountains will undergo a calamity by which their firmness, their cohesion, and their remaining fixed in their place will come to an end. It is possible that this whole process will begin with an actual earthquake. And the Qur'an itself explains that earthquake:

﴿When the earth is shaken with its violent shaking, and the earth brings forth its burdens.﴾ (99:1–2)

All these events will take place during the long day of Resurrection.

And when the pregnant camels, ten months gone, are left neglected [﴿وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾ (81:4)] ...

Al-'Ishar (العشار) refers to she-camels that are pregnant and have completed ten months of gestation. For the Arabs, there was no property more valuable than these. They took great care of them, because they were about to give birth, and then would give milk, and their benefit was near at hand. On the day these great upheavals take place, people will be so overcome with panic that they will abandon even such valuable property. No one will turn towards such precious wealth. The people to whom the Qur'an was addressed, especially the Arabs, would never have abandoned such property, unless some great calamity had befallen them.

And when the wild beasts are gathered together (81:5). These beasts, which flee from humans and even from one another, will be so terrified that they will gather in one place, instead of scattering across the mountains and retreating into their holes, caves and burrows, as is their habit. They will gather together in one place, feeling neither fear of humans nor of one another. Predators will forget their prey; they will run about in every direction and will not seek refuge in their caves, as they normally do when they enter such dens. Nor will a predator chase its prey, and this state will come about because all these beasts and birds will be frightened, and so they will abandon their very needs. If this is the condition of the animals, then what need be said of humans?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 81, verse 6:

﴿وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾ "And when the seas are filled up." The word sujjirat may also mean: the seas will be filled with water. It may also mean that the water will come into the seas in the same way as storms of clouds and rains attack the earth, when the earth has become cold and its crust has become hard, which we have mentioned in Surah an-Nazi'at. Or it means that when earthquakes occur in the earth and volcanic activity takes place, the land between the seas will disappear and the seas will rush upon one another. Or its meaning may be that they will catch fire and burst forth, as is mentioned elsewhere.

﴿وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ﴾ "And when the seas are burst open." The way the seas may burst open is that the components of water, hydrogen and oxygen, may come together in one place, or their components may split apart in the way that particles and atoms split. This form will be extremely terrifying. When this happens, an unimaginable fire will blaze in these seas. When a limited number of atomic or hydrogen explosions take place, they produce a terrible explosion, but if the particles of all the seas were to split apart, a human being cannot even imagine the enormous hell that would be created by that terrible explosion.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 81, verses 7–8:

"And when the souls are joined" (81:7). Its one meaning is that all souls will be joined with their bodies, and they will be reunited and brought back to life anew. It is also possible that the meaning is that people will be formed into groups of like kind, as is mentioned elsewhere.

"And you will be three groups" (56:7). That is, the group of those brought near to Allah, the people of the right hand, and the people of the left hand; or, according to some other principle of division, people will be joined together.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 81, verse 9:

﴿And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin she was killed.﴾ (81:8-9)

In the Age of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah), humanity had sunk to such a depth that the burying of daughters alive was a common practice among the people. They committed this act for two reasons. First, they considered it a disgrace that their daughters should become the wives or slave-girls of others. Second, they feared poverty and destitution. The Holy Qur'an recorded this evil custom of the Age of Ignorance for all time, by setting it down in writing. For Islam came precisely to rescue the Arabs and the whole of humanity from this degradation, and to grant humanity progress and exaltation. The Qur'an says:

﴿And when one of them is given the good news of a daughter, his face darkens and he is filled with suppressed anger. He hides himself from the people because of the bad news he has been given. Should he keep her in disgrace or bury her in the dust? Evil is the judgment they make.﴾ (16:58-59)

And in another place:

﴿And when one of them is given the good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as an example, his face darkens and he is filled with grief. Is one who is brought up in ornaments and is unable to express himself clearly in dispute [to be attributed to Allah]?﴾ (43:17-18)

And in a third place He said:

﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is a great sin.﴾ (17:31)

This custom was carried out in practice with great cruelty. The daughter would be buried alive. One form it took was that when the girl reached the age of six, her father would say to her mother, "Prepare the girl, I am taking her to her maternal uncle's house." Before this, he would already have dug a pit in some empty place. When he brought the girl to the pit, he would say, "Look into the well," and then push her into it and cover her with earth from above.

In some nations the practice was that when a woman's time of delivery came, she would be seated at the edge of a pit. If the child born was a daughter, she would throw it into the pit; and if it was a son, she would bring it home. If a family did not intend to bury its daughter alive, it would keep her in a most wretched condition, and when she became fit to herd camels, she would be dressed in a garment of wool or hair and sent out to the countryside to herd the camels.

Those who did not bury their daughters alive, and did not make them herd camels, would bury them alive by other means. When the poor woman was married and her husband died, the head of the family would come and throw a cloth over her head. This meant that no one could marry this woman. If he himself found her pleasing, he would marry her, whether she liked the marriage or not. If she did not please him, he would still keep her confined until she died, and he would inherit her property. Unless the woman freed herself by paying him her own wealth. Some men would divorce a woman on the condition that she could marry only where they willed, unless she freed herself from that condition by paying a ransom. Sometimes, if a husband died, they would keep the widow for the younger sons of the family. When a boy reached maturity, he would marry her. If there was an orphan girl under someone's guardianship, he would not let her marry, so that his guardianship would not end, and so that if his wife died he could marry her himself, or marry her to his young children. They did this only out of greed for wealth. Or, if the girl was beautiful, they would keep her back on account of her beauty.

In short, these were the days and nights of that poor woman in the Age of Ignorance. When Islam came, it strongly condemned all these customs and practices. It went to great lengths in condemning the burying of daughters alive, and it made clear that this would be one of the important questions raised on the field of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted has mentioned it among the terrifying scenes which will disrupt the entire order of this universe, as though it too was an event by which the social order is shaken. If the girl buried alive will be questioned as to why this act was done to her, then the person who committed this vile deed will certainly be questioned.

The truth is that in no jahili system could a woman attain a position of honour, had the Islamic Shariah and the Islamic system of life not granted dignity and honour to the human species, and had they not made men and women equal in this esteem and honour, and had they not said that Allah breathed His spirit into man. Then this honour would never have been bestowed upon women as Islam has bestowed it. A woman can obtain a life of honour and dignity only through the Islamic system. She cannot receive honour and dignity from any other agent or way of life, nor from any society.

Thus the new birth which humanity received came about through those values which were revealed from the heavens, and as a result of this, women too attained their station in this world. Therefore, because of women's natural weakness, the material needs of her life have been placed upon her husband, and by this her worth and value, and their weight and station, are in no way diminished. This is because in the Islamic system material life does not have such great importance. In the Islamic system the real weight lies with spiritual values, which are connected with Allah, and in respect of spiritual values there is no difference between men and women.

When the proofs are counted that this religion is from Allah, and that the Blessed Personality who presented this religion is the Messenger of Allah, then the station which Islam has given to women will be at the head of those proofs. For in the age in which Islam gave women this station, there was no sign, no movement, and no social demand, nor any such thing, that women should be given this station. There was no economic movement, and no social pressure, that women should be given this status. It was a purely Islamic system which accomplished this feat under pure divine revelation. Islam, solely in accordance with divine guidance, raised women out of that degradation of the Age of Ignorance to a lofty station, and completely transformed the circumstances of their lives.

"And when the records of deeds are laid open" (Surah al-Takwir, 81:10). The word ṣuḥuf (pages, records) here means the record of deeds. To be "laid open" (nushirat) means that the records of people's deeds will no longer remain hidden; they will be exposed fully before all people and will no longer be unintelligible. This very exposure will be a torment for wrongdoers, for there will be many secret evils which, if revealed, would bring great shame upon the evildoer, and he would be reduced to melting away; but what will his state be when all his deeds are before the people at that time?

The laying open of the records of deeds and the unveiling of secrets will also add to the terror of that day, and it will be a great upheaval in the worldly life, when secrets will be uncovered and the hidden matters that lie in hearts will also become manifest.

"And when the sky is stripped away" (81:11). The record of deeds consists of the circumstances of the earth; in contrast to them, the conditions of the heavens will also be laid bare. The first meaning of the word "sky" is that the blue canopy above our heads will be removed. How it will be removed, only Allah knows the manner. In any case, the blue dome that appears above our heads will not be seen, and a different scene will present itself.

And now the final scene, the last of the scenes of that Day:

"When the Fire is set blazing, and when Paradise is brought near" (81:12–13). That is, when the fire of Hell is kindled and made to blaze fiercely, its flames increase, and its roaring and heat intensify. Where is this Hell, and how will it be kindled? What kind of fuel will be used? On this matter we have only one verse:

"Its fuel will be men and stones" (2:24). This state will be when the people of Hell are thrown into it. And when Paradise is brought near, and those who are to enter Paradise see it before them, it will become clear to them that they will enter it with ease. In such a case it is called "muzlifah," that is, brought near, and in a state of being prepared and adorned, so that only a few steps remain to be taken, and even a few disordered steps can carry a person there.

When in this universe, in the realm of things, whether living beings or inanimate objects or plants, such a revolution takes place, then who will have any doubt that this stage is coming? Every person will surely recall his deeds, the deeds that he prepared for that Day, that he brings or presents, and that he readied for reckoning and for answering the reckoning.

﴿Every soul will know what it has brought forward﴾ (14:81). At that time every person will know what they have brought. On that terrifying day every person will know what they possess and what is owed by them. On that day a person will come to know this, and their condition will be one of trembling. They will also know that they can no longer alter or change anything in their record of deeds: nothing will be added to it and nothing will be reduced. They will come to know this at a time when they have been cut off from the world, and their notions about the future that they once held will be gone. They are severed from the world, and the world has moved away from them. Everything has changed, and everything has been transformed. Today, only the Being of the Lord remains, eternal and enduring. How good it would have been if people had turned towards the Lord in this world, so that on the Day of Resurrection, amid the changing circumstances, Allah would be present before them.

With these impactful allusions, this first paragraph concludes. It fills the human sentiment with a profound awareness, the scenes of the Resurrection settle in the human mind, and the transformation is complete.

Now the second paragraph begins. In it, attention is drawn to the most beautiful scenes of this universe. For this, extremely beautiful concepts have been chosen: what wahy (revelation) is, an oath is sworn upon it; the office of prophethood; and what the angels are like who bring it. The response of people to this Qur'an also lies within the sphere of the Divine will.

The Khunnas, the Jawari and the Kunnas: all three refer to the stars. The Khunnas are the stars that recede and return in their orbits; the Jawari are those that move along; and the Kunnas are those that hide. Through the figurative style of expression, these stars are given the qualities of living things, like deer, which turn, run and enter their lairs. They turn from one direction to another. These stars, as it were, appear living, running, wheeling about like living deer. The manner of expression gives the movement of these stars a grace of motion. And in their appearance too there is beauty; and in the atmosphere too there is its beauty. Their hiding is beautiful and their emerging is beautiful. Their running is good and their turning is good. Then the words are beautiful, and their pronunciation too is melodious, resonant and beautiful. Clearly, they neither hide nor do they come into view.

And the night when it darkens (81:17). But the word ʿasʿasa (عسعس) also carries a suggestion of meaning. ʿAs means moving about in darkness with hands and feet, when nothing can be seen with the eyes; it is as though the night is moving along in the darkness. This is an extremely beautiful mode of expression.

"And by the dawn when it breathes [its first breath]." This too is a living, even radiant, mode of expression, and it carries a great deal of suggestion. The break of dawn is, as it were, alive: it emerges by breathing. The light is, so to speak, the breath of the dawn, and the movement of beasts, birds and humans at dawn is the sign of its life. I can say with certainty that among the most beautiful modes of expression in the Arabic language there is no phrase more beautiful than this for the emergence of the dawn. A living and sensitive heart, on seeing the dawn, fully perceives that the dawn is breathing; and when such a heart then reads this verse of the Qur'an, it says that this too was in my heart.

Whoever has a taste for understanding the styles of speech, and can delight in fine scene-painting and picture-drawing, when he reads this verse:

﴿So, I swear by the receding stars, the ones that run and hide, and by the night when it darkens, and by the dawn when it breathes.﴾ (81:15–18)

will know that this passage contains a great store of meaning, insight and modes of expression within itself, and that the cosmic realities to which it points are beyond these. It appears that cosmic realities are taken up with a keen feeling and awareness.

These cosmic scenes, which have been clothed in life, and whose spirit has been joined with the human spirit through a living and beautiful style of expression, unveil to the human soul its true secrets and mysteries, and point to the power that is at work behind all these things. The scenes are the singers of the song of the faith-reality to which one is being called. Then this reality is presented in the most excellent circumstances, so that it may be remembered and human nature may welcome it.

"Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger, [possessing] power, held in high standing with the Lord of the Throne, obeyed there, [and] trustworthy" (81:19-21). That is, this Qur'an that is being presented to you, and especially these terrors of the Day of Resurrection that are being described, is the word of the noble Messenger, namely Jibreel (peace be upon him), who is the envoy of God and who conveyed this message safely. The Qur'an is thus, in one sense, the word of God, and then also the word of Jibreel (peace be upon him), who repeated it as the message of God.

And the bearer of this message, to whom the responsibility of bringing this important message down from the heavens was entrusted, what kind of personality is he? He is extremely honored with God, and God's statement is that he is possessed of very firm capabilities. This also shows that the angel charged with conveying the message of the Qur'an needed to be granted the ability to perform that task. His rank with God is elevated, he is honored and close to the Lord of the Mighty Throne, and he is trustworthy and reliable, one who conveys fully what has been given to him and is able to convey it.

From their attributes it is evident that this speech is of the utmost importance and holds a lofty, high station. It also shows how greatly God has favored mankind, in appointing for the guidance of humanity such a messenger to bring down the Qur'an, who conveys this message to the chosen Prophet. This favor and kindness is so great that if a person reflects upon it, he would melt with shame at how the Lord of the worlds shows such generosity to humanity: among God's creation, man is honored, the message that came upon him is honored, the angel who brought it is honored, and the Prophet upon whom it descended, the chosen Prophet, is honored.

These are the qualities of the messenger who brought the word of God and handed it to the chosen Prophet. As for the status of the Messenger who came to the people with this message, he is your companion and brother. He lived among you for a long time. Therefore it is strange that when he came to you with this exalted speech, you hurled accusations at him and adopted various attitudes toward him, although he is your companion, about whom you have full knowledge, and in conveying to you the unseen matters he tells you, he is most trustworthy.

﴿Your companion is not mad. He certainly saw him on the clear horizon. And he is not stingy with the unseen. And this is not the word of an accursed devil. So where are you going? This is nothing but a reminder to the worlds, to whichever of you wishes to take the straight path. And you will not wish, unless Allah, the Lord of the worlds, wills.﴾ (81:22–29)

The people of Makkah knew a great deal about the Holy Prophet (ﷺ). They knew that he was a highly intelligent man, truthful and trustworthy, steadfast and upon the right path. Yet despite this, they said that he was mad, and that the things he said were being whispered to him by a devil. They carried out these claims as a conspiracy against the Holy Prophet (ﷺ), and the details of this are found in the books of hadith (traditions of the Prophet (ﷺ)). Some of them, overawed by the exalted speech of the Qur'an, did this even while acknowledging that no human could produce such speech. They had not heard such speech from any human being. They also held the belief that every poet has a devil attached to him, who inspires his poetry. They further believed that soothsayers (kahin) also have devils attached to them, who whisper unseen matters to them. It was also common among them that sometimes a devil attaches itself to certain people and speaks its own words through their tongues. However, they were in no way prepared to interpret and explain this exalted speech correctly, namely that it comes from the Lord of the worlds.

In this passage, therefore, the Qur'an drew their attention to the beauty of the universe. It invited them to reflect upon the living and radiant sights of this universe, and through them it sought to establish in their minds the idea that this Qur'an, like the universe, is a unique and incomparable speech, and that it comes from the One who created this universe. Just as He placed beauty in the universe, He has placed beauty in the Qur'an too, which has no equal. The Qur'an then described the qualities of the angel who bears the Qur'an and of the Messenger who conveys it. It said that this Messenger is your companion, whom you know. There is no quality of madness in him. He saw with his own eyes the angel who brought this speech to him. At that time the angel was spread across the horizon, and the Messenger had certain knowledge (haqq al-yaqin) that this was an angel, sent by the Lord of the worlds, and that whatever knowledge of the unseen is brought to him, he conveys with complete trustworthiness. There is nothing doubtful in these matters. Indeed, you yourselves have never heard any false word from the Messenger of Allah.

﴿وما هو ............................ رجيم﴾ (25:81) "And it is not the word of an accursed devil."

This is because Satan does not point people to a straight path of this kind. Allah the Exalted asks, in a tone of warning, "Where are you going?"

Then where are you going? (81:26)

"Then where are you going?" How wrong are your judgments, and how foolish are your words! Turning away from the truth, where are you heading? Yet the truth and the straight path lie right before you.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 81, verse 27:

﴿ان هو إلا ذكر للعالمين﴾ (81:27) "It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds." This is a reminder, and it tells them what the reality of their existence is, what the purpose of their creation is, and what the purpose of the universe spread around them is. This call is a universal call. Although this call is currently surrounded by enemies, in reality it is a worldwide movement. This verse is a testimony that the Islamic call was, from its very beginning, a universal call.

After this, they are told that guidance and admonition are attained by those who resolve to move forward towards it. Since Allah has provided you with these facilities, now what is needed is that you make up your mind and set out on this path. If you do not walk on it, you will be held accountable.

"For whoever among you wills to take the straight path" — that is, whoever intends to take the guidance, who wishes to walk toward Allah. For after this discourse there remains no doubt that the path of Allah is the straight path. After this discourse and reminder, all excuses fall away, because this discourse makes the right path clear to a sound and upright heart. Therefore, whoever now deviates from the right path will be held to account.

The truth is that the signs of faith and the proofs of guidance, in the self and in the horizons, are so abundant that every person barely manages to extricate himself from their sphere of influence, and for that he must make a deliberate effort. The powerful impact of these proofs remains upon every person at all times. Especially the one who reflects upon the Qur'an and understands the highly effective eloquence of the Qur'an's discourse, and all those who hear and comprehend the Qur'an. They will deviate from the path of truth deliberately, and they will never have any reasonable excuse or justification.

When it has been made clear that it is possible for all people to come onto the path of guidance, and it has also been made clear that Allah has made the path of truth easy for everyone, then at this point it was deemed appropriate to also clearly tell people the great reality operating behind their wish: that even if they want to, they cannot come onto the straight path without the divine grace of Allah (tawfiq).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 81, verse 29:

"And you do not will except that Allah wills, the Lord of the worlds." This is so that they do not think that their will is independent of and separate from the all-encompassing will of Allah, to which all affairs return. The granting of choice by Allah, and the facilitating of the path of guidance, are also confined within the great will of Allah, within whose circle are confined all matters that have occurred and all that are yet to occur.

This verse, and all other similar verses in which the will of people is immediately followed by the statement that what happens is only what Allah wills, are revealed so that people's conceptions of the generality and all-encompassing nature of Allah's will may be corrected. This is a great reality, and its summary is that all affairs are within the sphere of Allah's will. And the free choices that Allah has given to people are within the circle of His wider will. For example, Allah has granted the angels the capacity to carry out Allah's commands; He has also given them permission to do so, and the ability to be able to do so. So it is also an aspect of Allah's will that they choose whichever of two paths they wish, and that they exercise this choice after instruction and explanation.

Believers should affirm this reality in their faith and their conceptions, so that they know what the true reality is. Seeing the supreme will of Allah, they should rely upon Allah alone, seek Allah's grace, and in whatever path they adopt or abandon, have the power and will of Allah before them.
